newsitem.title: SPAIN: Tabacalera shares slide after Liggett deal.
newsitem.headline: Tabacalera shares slide after Liggett deal.

text.p: Shares in Spanish tobacco company Tabacalera took a tumble on Friday after U.S. firm Liggett Group struck a settlement deal and admitted the hazards of smoking.
By 1300 GMT, Tabacalera shares were 50 pesetas down at 6,680, while the Ibex-35 index of leading shares was up 35.02, or 0.65 percent, up at 5,390.48.
"Tabacalera is suffering from the impact of the Liggett Group deal," a dealer said. "But the market is also not very liquid."
On Thursday, U.S. tobacco company Liggett Group, agreed to settle with the attorney generals of 22 states who have sued the industry to recoup the Medicaid health care costs of treating smokers.
They have agreed to hand over documents which could prove devastating for the whole industry.
Liggett, owned by Bennett LeBow's Brooke Group, also became the first company to admit the health hazards of smoking admitting that it was addictive.
Legal experts have said the action could result in a flood of legal actions against tobacco companies.
